title: The Penalty That Took a Name
coreQuestion: What made Panenka's 1976 penalty so audacious?

facts.claim: The UEFA Euro 1976 final between Czechoslovakia and West Germany was played in Belgrade.
Czechoslovakia won the final on penalties.
Hoeneß's penalty went over the bar, giving Panenka the chance to win the title.
Panenka feigned shooting to the side, Sepp Maier dived, and Panenka gently chipped the ball into the middle of the net.
A Panenka is a penalty in which the taker delicately chips the ball over a diving goalkeeper.

narration.text: This penalty won a European Championship.
West Germany's Uli Hoeneß sent his kick over the bar.
Then Antonín Panenka stepped up, and the goalkeeper dived.
Panenka chipped it, gently, into the middle of the net.
A kick so cheeky it now carries his name. Every goal has a story.
